newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cluff says recovers 56 diamonds from mine.
newsitem.headline: Cluff says recovers 56 diamonds from mine.

text.p: Diamond exploration company Cluff Resources Pacific NL said on Wednesday it has recovered 56 gem quality diamonds from its "Streak of Luck" mine in Copeton, New South Wales.

"Treatment of the initial stockpile of basal rocks from the Streak of Luck open pit at Copeton has been partially completed, with the recovery of 56 gem quality diamonds, including one fancy yellow gem weighing 1.10 carats," the company told the Australian Stock Exchange.
Two other diamonds were in excess of three quarters of a carat in weight, and an additional five in excess of half a carat, Cluff said.
The diamonds recovered averaged about four to the carat, the company said.
Treatment of further quantities of rocks currently underway would determine whether the recovery of diamonds from the open pit is of economic significance, Cluff said.
The latest recoveries bring to 145 the number of gem-quality diamonds found so far at the mine, Peter Kennewell, a Cluff director said.
